findings.description: The approved build sequence misses the §1.a default-transport deliverable.
findings.failureScenario: A staff/fresh install follows the completed framework and still gets the packaged `api` transport default because the shipped `router-config.yaml` is package data and `resolve_transport()` falls through to that value/default. That is probable because no session in the approved sequence assigns changing the shipped config/staff default, while the current packaged config explicitly says `profile: api`.

findings.description: Pricing removal is incomplete; the sequence covers arithmetic/checks but not the shipped rate-table/config/schema surfaces the spec says must go.
findings.failureScenario: Session 8 can delete `pricing.py` arithmetic and the load-time rate check exactly as written while leaving rate fields, `confirmed_on`, schema support, and dollar-cost reporting in place. That is probable because those surfaces exist today and the approved sequence names only `pricing.py` arithmetic and the load-time check, not the packaged config/schema/metrics cleanup.

findings.description: The sequence does not assign enforcement of “planning-only” human overrides, while current code can waive ordinary code sessions.
findings.failureScenario: A future code session reaches the review/adjudication impasse path and an operator runs `verify waive`; the command writes a non-blocking `WAIVED` row and stamps the session verification without checking that the session is a planning session. That is probable because the existing CLI advertises and implements this path generally, and no planned session removes or restricts it.

findings.description: The waiver guard is assigned to Session 4, leaving Session 3 able to use the existing ordinary-code waiver path.
findings.failureScenario: Session 3 reaches the verification cap with an upheld blocking finding. Because Session 4 has not run yet, today’s `verify waive` still permits an interactive operator to stamp `WAIVED` on that ordinary code session; the close gate then treats it as non-blocking. This is probable because Session 3 is the very next code session, and the current code/tests explicitly support waiver after upheld adjudication for a normal session.

findings.description: The waiver remediation still misses the run-core `finish --waive` approval path.
findings.failureScenario: A staff code session using the run-core verified policy hits a blocking review, then an operator runs `dabbler finish --run <id> --waive "shipping anyway" --attest-operator`; today that path returns `WAIVED` and records the finish. This is probable because the public parser exposes `finish --waive`, and the test suite explicitly asserts it works for `Session 2: Review the parser`, whose fixture text is ordinary implementation work.

findings.description: The “no approval anywhere” design still leaves Session 3 instructed to preserve planning-session waivers.
findings.failureScenario: Session 3 follows its explicit step 2 and adds only a “not ordinary code” guard, leaving `verify waive` / `finish --waive` usable for planning sessions. Planning sessions are exactly the likely cap-hit case the docs cite, so a future capped plan can still be operator-waived even though the new spec says no person can type a verdict.

findings.description: The waiver removal is still scheduled before a usable cap-terminal path exists for sessions 4–9.
findings.failureScenario: Session 4–9 reaches the verification cap after waiver removal. Because Session 3 only says to add the replacement state while Session 10 “wires it into the loop,” the current pre-Session-10 verification paths still either pause/refuse at the cap or keep close blocked on the latest blocking round. This is probable because every intervening session must run cross-provider verification, and this very session already hit the cap.

findings.description: **Nit:** `docs/session-sets/148-the-session-framework/spec.md:418-419` still says Session 10 “Creates” the terminal state, even though Session 10’s steps now correctly say Session 3 built/wired it and Session 10 adds nothing new. This is a stale summary line, not a blocking sequencing defect.
